decisions.reason: As an adjustable cardboard display very close to our core display know-how, it fits existing production and design capabilities and can be improved through our in-house R&D rather than withdrawn quickly.

The pegboard-back cardboard display remains strongly related to our established offer, so our absorptive capacity for design, testing, and customer feedback is high and supports keeping it on the market.
This quarter-pallet cardboard display is well within our existing competence base, and although it overlaps with nearby variants, we are more likely to refine or reposition it than drop it outright.
The eighth-pallet format is a familiar extension of our shelf-display business, making it easy for us to assess demand and adapt the product using current knowledge and assets.

The wooden display pallet is somewhat less aligned with our core paper-based expertise, so the risk of withdrawal is higher, but its adjacency to our display business and our development capabilities still favor retention for now.

This media-focused cardboard quarter-pallet display is still close to our main offer, and our established customer relationships and in-house development make continued learning and commercial adjustment more likely than exit.
